coverage.remaining: None. The whole document was read, narrative, footnotes and all seven appendices.
coverage.note: A 23-page statement whose narrative is thin on numbered addresses and whose appendices are dense with them. Three seams carry the whole yield. The footnotes to the narrative (nn. 4-17) are where the venues get their street numbers — the prose names the bar and the footnote gives the address and the years, so a reader who skips the footnotes gets almost nothing. Appendix C, page 17, is a scanned table of 21 North Beach bars and restaurants 1933-1965, each with an address and a date range. Appendix D, page 18, is the scanned key to a South of Market site map 1960-1993, 67 numbered locations carrying about 140 separate business tenancies, each dated. Appendices A, B, E and F are maps with no street numbers on them and yield nothing: E is a schematic of 16th Street with venue names but no addresses, and F is a numbered Tenderloin site map whose key was not reproduced with it. Appendix G lists five landmarks by name without addresses; only Castro Camera could be tied to a number, from the narrative. Pages 17-20 have no text layer at all — pdftotext returns the heading and nothing else — so the appendices were read as rendered page images. The document contradicts itself three times, and each contradiction is recorded on the findings rather than resolved: California Hall is 600 Polk in the narrative and 625 Polk in the church list; the Society for Individual Rights is at 67 Sixth Street in one footnote and 83 Sixth Street in another; and Mona's 440 closes in 1948 in Appendix C and 1949 in footnote 5.
